note: Built by scripts/build_crops.py from walo-crops.json (team crop knowledge base). Values keep their source ids; 'not confirmed' means no source was found. EcoCrop ranges are global, not Ghana-specific.

ejura_sekyedumase.name: Ejura-Sekyedumase (Ashanti)
ejura_sekyedumase.note: FAO describes the Transitional zone as the northern parts of Ashanti and Brong-Ahafo.

techiman.name: Techiman (Bono East, formerly Brong-Ahafo)
techiman.note: Mapped by FAO's region description (northern Brong-Ahafo); Techiman sits near the forest–transition boundary – verify locally.

tamale.name: Tamale (Northern Region)
tamale.note: FAO: Guinea savanna covers Northern, Upper East and Upper West; single rainy season Jun–Oct.

excluded.why: Wild parkland tree: not a planting recommendation (walo-crops.json confidence: low).

ranking.method: See data/rules.json (methods with sources) and DESIGN.md Methods.
ranking.confidence_rule: Ejura, Techiman and Tamale use the team's per-crop rating. Other places: Transitional → the higher of Ejura/Techiman; Guinea savanna → Tamale; Rain forest / Coastal savanna → Medium if FAO gives dated windows for that zone, else Low; at least Medium where FAO's zone description names the crop. Places outside FAO's zone text (Dambai) are ranked on NASA climate only and marked Best guess.

facts.value: Extra-early 75–85 d; early 90–95 d; medium 105–110 d; late >110 d (e.g. Obatanpa 110 d, CSIR-Omankwa 90 d, CSIR-Abontem 75–80 d)

facts.label: Rain needs
facts.value: Ghana guides give no single mm figure; maize is sensitive to moisture stress at flowering. See EcoCrop for global mm thresholds.

facts.label: Temperature
facts.value: Optimum 30–34 °C for growth (MoFA, IITA); germination fastest 28–32 °C; yields fall if high temperature coincides with pollen shedding.

facts.label: Heat stress
facts.value: Each degree-day above 30 °C cut African maize trial yields by ~1% (optimal rain-fed) and ~1.7% (drought).

facts.label: Drought
facts.value: Moderate–low: sensitive at flowering; drought-tolerant varieties exist (e.g. CSIR-Sanzal-sima, Wang-dataa, Bihilifa).

facts.label: Soil
facts.value: Well-drained, well-aerated, deep loamy soils with organic matter; avoid sandy, gravelly, shallow and waterlogged soils; pH 5.0–7.0.

facts.label: Pests & diseases
facts.value: Fall armyworm, African armyworm, stem borer (Busseola fusca), Striga, larger grain borer (storage); maize streak virus, rusts; aflatoxin (Aspergillus) contamination.

facts.label: Yields in Ghana
facts.value: National avg ~2.5–2.8 t/ha (FAOSTAT 2020–2024); variety potential 4.6–9.0 t/ha on-station.

facts.value: Requires less rainfall than most crops; heavy rain encourages vegetative growth and disease; needs dry weather at harvest.

facts.label: Soil
facts.value: Best on well-drained sandy loams; sensitive to waterlogging on heavy clays.
